scenario: Both employees accept a valid same-week trade
expected: Exactly both owners change in one transaction; one terminal result; dates, locations, positions and Lead duties stay attached to their slots.

scenario: Target declines before acceptance
expected: Neither assignment changes; terminal decline recorded; pending reminders cancelled.

scenario: Requester cancels while target accepts
expected: One serialized outcome wins; never half a swap or success after a committed cancellation.

scenario: Target employee is wrong, caller forges requester or tries self-swap
expected: Server rejects without changing either assignment or disclosing private request data.

scenario: Source equals target or the owning weeks differ
expected: Current same-shift/same-week restrictions are enforced server-side; no new cross-week feature.

scenario: Manager changes a consent-bound date/time/location/position/Lead/owner
expected: Old consent is rejected; a fresh request is required rather than silently applying changed terms.

scenario: Only the employee display name changes
expected: No fabricated consent failure for unchanged terms; current presentation and historical identity remain accurate.

scenario: The applicable swap/coverage approval mode is disabled, missing or legacy/manual
expected: Valid consent follows the established manual path; no assignment changes or retroactive auto-completion. Missing mandatory notice/rule data is reported rather than assumed.

scenario: Two outgoing shifts would otherwise appear as conflicts
expected: Validate each employee against the correct final ledger with only their outgoing assignment removed.

scenario: One side of a proposed trade violates a rule
expected: Neither side is applied; safe explanation identifies the failure without leaking peer private facts.

scenario: Ordinary owner offers future published shift
expected: One OPEN offer; original assignment stays until replacement; no implied absence approval.

scenario: Two eligible employees claim the same offer concurrently
expected: One valid transaction commits; loser sees unavailable; exactly one replacement and one completion event.

scenario: Invalid candidate claims then valid candidate claims
expected: Invalid attempt does not reserve/close the shift; valid candidate can still complete.

scenario: Original owner attempts to claim own offer
expected: Rejected without assignment or status mutation.

scenario: Manager-policy claim is later withdrawn
expected: No completed assignment is undone; current version is checked; closure/reoffer follows P09.

scenario: A pending inability-to-work report is submitted
expected: Existing assignment is retained with an explicit operational risk; private reason only available to authorized parties.

scenario: Manager approves callout with no replacement yet
expected: Original employee is released in existing ledger semantics; one linked OPEN coverage need remains visibly unfilled.

scenario: Replacement accepts coverage for approved callout
expected: Replacement owns shift and counts once; original absence history remains; release flag does not transfer to replacement.

scenario: Replacement later submits their own callout on the same shift
expected: Historic original callout is retained but does not permanently block new owner; active release matches assignment episode.

scenario: Callout approval/cancellation races with accepted coverage or a trade
expected: No replacement is removed, no new duplicate need appears, and no absent owner is silently restored.

scenario: Callout plus existing coverage/trade participates in the same source slot
expected: Record the genuine inability report; resolve incompatible participation atomically, preserve history and committed replacements, and keep only one linked coverage need.

scenario: Urgent inability is reported after shift start
expected: Manager reporting remains available with clear limitations; no past/full-shift automatic transfer or punch mutation.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Current employee, account, location or workspace becomes inactive
expected: No new automatic assignment; safe cancellations/history remain possible within authorization.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Candidate lacks location eligibility or a required active position
expected: Discovery and final completion reject candidate using shared validation.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Multi-qualified candidate covers a single-position slot

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Required designated Lead would be lost

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Normal availability plus submitted weekly snapshot/exceptions
expected: Preserve shared precedence, intentionally empty submissions and partial-day unavailable gaps.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Pending versus approved time off
expected: Use existing shared status semantics; approved leave blocks; nonblocking states do not become invented blockers.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Cross-location conflict and same-day limit
expected: Automatic mode enforces full ledger/daily policy, not the more permissive manual warning path.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Target 24, configured weekly max 40; projected 32, 40 and 41 scheduled hours
expected: 32/40 remain eligible under other rules; 41 violates this configured cap. The message identifies a scheduling cap, not a universal legal prohibition or final overtime-pay conclusion.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Sunday overnight shift crosses Monday
expected: Evaluate availability/leave and maximum hours in both business workweeks; exclude outgoing work correctly.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Owning schedule week differs from touched business date
expected: Locks, ledger and publication associations use their proper identities; no omitted carry-in/out.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Workspace timezone differs from browser/Mac timezone
expected: Same valid operational result for same persisted workspace facts.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: DST gap, repeated civil time or malformed legacy boundary
expected: Use strict existing boundary policy; no guessed instant or silent 00:00 substitution.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Unrelated location lacks setup
expected: It does not block a valid requested slot; a requested inactive/unready location cannot auto-complete.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Existing unrelated staffing gap versus new affected gap
expected: Do not require fixing unrelated week defects; never introduce/worsen affected staff/position/Lead gaps.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Ranking uses zero/missing/mixed targets and shuffled input order
expected: No fabricated target or division errors; final shared fairness semantics and rotating tie remain deterministic.

group: Shared rules, ranking and business time
scenario: Highly ranked employee does not volunteer
expected: No assignment or extra hours without explicit acceptance; rank is not consent.

scenario: Same shift is source in one request and target in another
expected: Cross-role exclusivity holds; separate-column indexes are not treated as sufficient proof.

scenario: Two opposite or chained swaps race
expected: Deterministic lock order and participation guard allow only compatible outcomes; no deadlock loop or double commitment.

scenario: Leave or availability insert occurs during acceptance
expected: Absent-row/phantom change is caught under both writer orders; no stale automatic assignment.

scenario: New assignment at another location changes candidate hours during acceptance
expected: Complete affected-ledger validation/guard catches overlap or maximum breach.

scenario: Position membership, max-hours policy or session role changes during lock wait
expected: Fresh final guard rejects lost authority or invalid scheduling facts.

scenario: Manager edits/deletes/unpublishes while acceptance waits
expected: No overwrite of new manager intent, no phantom assignment and no publication of a draft.

scenario: Phase 4 generation/manual input writers race with Phase 5
expected: Shared lock ordering and source guards hold; no deadlocks from independent lock conventions.

scenario: Same action is submitted twice with the same operation identity
expected: Return same persisted result; one assignment change, revision and visible completion event.

scenario: Same operation identity is reused with different terms or another account
expected: Reject key misuse; no replay across actor/workspace boundaries.

scenario: Transport fails after successful commit
expected: Reconcile recorded command outcome before retry; no second swap or falsely definite failure.

scenario: Recognized source conflict/deadlock/serialization failure
expected: One bounded retry owner rereads and reevaluates; permission/deadline/unknown errors are not blindly retried.

scenario: Failure is injected between each mutation stage
expected: All assignments, request state, participation, history, revisions and intents roll back together.

scenario: A source row is later deleted or reassigned
expected: Request history retains original parties/terms/outcome; cascades or live joins do not erase/misattribute it.

scenario: Generated-origin assignment is changed by a completed exchange
expected: Protected human-controlled provenance is retained; genuine actor/mode recorded; no tombstone auto-clear.

scenario: Claim just before, exactly at, and after the effective completion cutoff
expected: Only before-cutoff final authorization can complete; apply the recorded/tighter current policy and shift-start upper bound using authoritative instants, not just dates.

scenario: Request begins before its effective cutoff but obtains locks afterward
expected: Post-wait policy/version/deadline guard rejects stale acceptance; no transfer, revision or completion notification is committed.

scenario: Worker does not run or runs after configured deadlines
expected: Expired actions remain invalid under effective policy; reads show truthful state; an accepted request is not confused with a closed creation window; unattended escalation is not claimed active.

scenario: Two worker ticks expire/escalate same request
expected: One durable event per lifecycle/stage; no duplicate reminders or assignments.

scenario: Acceptance and expiry worker race
expected: Single serialized outcome; expired request never acquires a replacement afterward.

scenario: Request created within urgent window
expected: One immediate applicable manager escalation; no waiting for an already-passed threshold.

scenario: No candidate exists or all invitees decline/dismiss
expected: Truthful unresolved need; bounded manager escalation; no involuntary assignment or repeated invite spam.

scenario: Worker crashes between preparation and commit or restarts mid-batch
expected: Stable cursor/idempotency recovers without losing or duplicating due work; no provider call inside business transaction.

scenario: Coverage opens with mixed eligible/ineligible employees
expected: Only current authorized eligible audience can receive actionable invitation; no personal callout details.

scenario: Valid trade/coverage updates both request and published revision
expected: Coalesced visible completion per recipient/transaction; required internal records remain complete.

scenario: Request cancelled after delivery lease claimed but before send
expected: Worker revalidates source and cancels stale action; already delivered pushes open a safe current state.

scenario: Same-state revision, new linked offer or legacy status-version event
expected: Version identity/cancellation remain correct; no stale event reuse, lost new event or notification-budget reset from repeated reoffers.

scenario: Caller tampers with employee/workspace/role/eligible/max-hours/Lead fields
expected: Strict server-derived authority; reject business-field injection and duplicate scalar parameters.

scenario: Real framework-generated Server Action form envelope
expected: Legitimate submission works; framework metadata handling cannot authorize forged business fields.

scenario: Unrelated employee, wrong request recipient or Lead accesses manager action directly
expected: Rejected server-side regardless of hidden buttons or client route.

scenario: Actor logs out/switches account while opening a request notification
expected: No cross-account private data or unauthorized mutation; safe return/deep-link behavior.

scenario: Employee eligibility revoked after invitation creation
expected: Dispatch/open/accept reevaluate applicable access and eligibility; invitation never guarantees acceptance.

scenario: Quiet hours, notification preferences, expired token or provider outage
expected: Honor approved policy; preserve business result; report delivery separately from assignment success.

scenario: Push delivery flags off and fake provider enabled for tests
expected: No real notification transport; durable local intent behavior tested and labeled accurately.

scenario: Sensitive reason note appears in candidate list, general history, URL, cache or push
expected: Test fails; reason is visible only to requester and authorized management.

scenario: Automatic completion through actual authenticated app and disposable DB
expected: Both real schedules and request/count/acknowledgement views refresh; not just a mocked button result.

scenario: Open, manual pending, released-unfilled, completed, expired and already-taken states
expected: Labels and available actions match persisted state; no stale manager approval or success banners.

scenario: Offline, loading, pending, error, no candidates and uncertain commit
expected: Useful truthful UI; no cached private data or deferred automatic acceptance; safe input preserved.

scenario: Long names/positions/locations at all seven widths and both engines
expected: Full text fits before horizontal scrolling; stable >=44px controls and explicit position/Lead context.

scenario: Keyboard and screen-reader interaction
expected: Correct focus/order/names/live feedback; dialogs restore focus; status not communicated by color alone.

scenario: Bottom-nav safe area and final action on mobile
expected: Action remains visible and reachable above fixed navigation; pending geometry does not jump.

scenario: Protected Manager/Employee/Lead/Login/Activate/PWA/Clocker surfaces
expected: No unintended changes; focused source-aware comparisons; no actual punches or provider activation.

scenario: Legacy request upgrade and missing schema
expected: History/policy preserved; no automatic conversion of MANAGER_PENDING; missing schema is an error, not an empty list.

scenario: Duplicate/inconsistent legacy participation and repeated callout episodes
expected: Migration rehearsal reports/resolves explicitly without deleting history or reassigning real employees.

scenario: Separate approval modes or applicable rules change while requests remain active
expected: Disabling/tightening applies at final guard; enabling/loosening neither bulk-completes existing manual requests nor extends prior consent/deadlines; changed rule facts are revalidated.

scenario: Migration compatibility rollback and restart
expected: Documented tested application/schema compatibility; no destructive drop/rewrite to fake reversibility.

scenario: Final branch review and handoff
expected: Approved base, exact commit, clean worktree, evidence, owned teardown and explicit no-push/no-deploy stop are recorded.

scenario: Independent swap and coverage approval modes
expected: Exercise automatic swaps/manual coverage and manual swaps/automatic coverage. Persist each independently; unauthorized toggles fail; the unrelated workflow and existing pending requests do not change.

scenario: Missing or partially migrated policy configuration
expected: Old/manual behavior remains recognizable; auto-completion is withheld where required settings are unknown. No implicit enabled flag, zero notice or not-applicable classification is invented.

scenario: Separate request and completion deadlines
expected: With fictional 24-hour submission/2-hour completion cutoffs, test both boundaries. A request created in time stays actionable until its completion cutoff; new requests after their own cutoff are refused. Values are fixtures, not customer defaults.

scenario: Explicit zero notice versus NULL and urgent inability reporting
expected: Only an explicitly configured zero cutoff permits action up to but not at shift start. Missing values are not zero. Genuine urgent callouts still reach management after trading closes, without backdated transfers.

scenario: Notice policy tightens or loosens during a lock wait
expected: A tighter effective deadline wins after the wait. Loosening never silently extends recorded consent/expiry or reopens a closed request. Worker, command and read projections agree.

scenario: Minimum rest against prior and next cross-location commitments
expected: Using fictional rest limits, reject a nonoverlapping but insufficient-rest assignment on either side. Remove outgoing shifts correctly; include adjacent days/workweeks and follow the defined time basis.

scenario: Per-shift and daily-hour maximums differ from weekly maximum
expected: A candidate below the weekly cap can still fail a daily/per-shift cap. Test the configured calendar or rolling window explicitly and reject unsupported/ambiguous semantics rather than guessing.

scenario: Replacement has different required break conditions
expected: Recheck authoritative incoming-employee break conditions, retaining shift and consent-bound terms. Missing or incompatible required facts withhold auto-completion; never remove a break, deduct pay or fabricate a waiver/punch to make the trade pass.

scenario: Required rule is unknown versus explicitly reviewed not applicable
expected: Unknown required facts cannot become an eligible result or a generic manager override. Authorized correction plus revalidation is required. An explicit reviewed not-applicable classification behaves differently from missing data.

scenario: Projected overtime threshold differs from target and hard cap
expected: In a fictional profile with target 24, threshold 40 and cap 44, projected 42 is a threshold crossing, not a cap breach; route according to configured review policy. Projected 45 still violates the cap. Do not seed these values or calculate final payroll.

scenario: Known hard failure versus an explicitly permitted soft exception
expected: Employee consent and manager review cannot bypass a known hard cap, required safety rule, forged consent or unresolved mandatory fact. Only already-permitted soft exceptions can be manually resolved; preserve reasons/history.

scenario: Shared policy parity across discovery, acceptance and affected consumers
expected: Verify one source of rule meaning across suggestions, final writes and touched manual/generation consumers, allowing only documented mode-specific exceptions. No copied rest/hour/break engine and no changes to the approved Phase 4 worktree.

scenario: Actual app, policy changes, privacy and legacy upgrade
expected: Use authenticated disposable-data flows to prove rule/mode/deadline updates, version guards, safe reasons and truthful pending states. No peer disclosure of private rule classification, universal compliance badge or migration-triggered activation.

scenario: Time-basis and actual-time evidence are not interchangeable
expected: Exercise daylight-saving elapsed rest versus nominal scheduled hours and absent actual-work data. Follow defined semantics or withhold unverifiable automation. Never infer final overtime owed, actual break completion or legal compliance from the scheduled ledger.
